text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and gateway timeouts observed for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error spike started ~1729993300. Auto-rate-limiter triggered. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

carla: Ack. I'm on call. Gathering initial scope. Which customer traffic is driving this?

dmitri: I can take this if needed, stepping in 2m. Any hot routes?

emma: Seeing a lot of 504s from the gateway layer and 503s from runtime. TL;DR: batching scheduler queue length > 12k across pool-3, head-of-line blocking visible.

carla: Thanks. Emma — can you paste the scheduler queue snapshot and the batching histo?

emma: Sure — from runtime-metrics: 
```
scheduler.queue.length: 12540
scheduler.inflight_batches: 820
batcher.pending_time_p95: 1.9s
batcher.pending_time_p99: 6.3s
kv_cache.size_gb: 72GB (growing)
kv_cache.evictions: 0/5m
```
Looks like KV cache growth + long prefix scans causing batcher to hold batches.

ben: We're seeing customer-facing errors: a few high-traffic customers (acme-payments, mailstream) reporting elevated latency and 5xx bursts. Support already opened an incident with ACME.

carla: Impact note for postmortem: ~6% 5xx across production for last 10m, top percentile on long-context routes.

dmitri: Hypothesis: KV cache GC/eviction isn't keeping up, causing blocking when scheduler tries to attach large KV contexts. Also some client traffic sent large sequence lengths that force big allocations.

sre-runner: Automatic mitigation options: (1) enable fallback-model for high-latency routes, (2) throttling for noisy customers, (3) manual kv-cache eviction / prefix pruning, (4) scale out pool-3. Which do we want live?

carla: Prioritize quick mitigations that don't require infra scaling first. Step 1: Enable per-customer throttles for ACME and mailstream. Step 2: Route non-critical traffic to smaller model-variants. Step 3: Trigger KV cache eviction pass.

emma: Doing throttles now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/throttle -d '{"customer":"acme-payments","rate":0.6}'` — throttle API accepted. Applying for mailstream as well.

ops-bot: ACTION LOG: throttle applied for acme-payments (0.6) and mailstream (0.5) by emma at 1729993412.

carla: Good. Next — fallback route. Ben, can you open a temporary route rule to send traffic hitting long_context route to model-small-1 until healthy?

ben: On it. Pushing route: `routeset apply --patch long_context: {fallback: model-small-1}`. Deployed in 30s.

emma: Route change propagated to gateway. Observing drop in head-of-line wait for a subset of requests. scheduler.queue length now 8230.

dmitri: I'll run a manual KV eviction sweep on pool-3 nodes (non-destructive): `runtime-admin kvcache --evict --age-threshold=3600`. Running across shards.

sre-runner: Note: running eviction will cause transient CPU spike on runtime daemons. Watch for extra 5xx during eviction window.

emma: Eviction started 1729993478 on pool-3 shards. Progress: shard0 100%, shard1 95%, shard2 100%. KV cache back down to 42GB. Evictions recorded: 8k keys.

carla: Nice. Any change in error rate?

ops-bot: METRICS: 5xx rate decreased from 6.2% -> 2.1% over last 3m. Gateway 504s trending down. avg p95 latency down 420ms.

dmitri: Queue length now 2100, inflight_batches 490. Head-of-line looks improved but still some hotspots. Suggest setting batcher.max_batch_size=32 and lowering batcher.wait_ms to 20ms for pool-3 as temporary config.

ben: I can roll that config. Applying `config apply --service=batcher --pool=pool-3 --set max_batch_size=32,wait_ms=20` now.

emma: Config applied. Watching. Batcher pending_time_p99 dropped to 1.1s, queue length to 900.

carla: Good progress. Notify support and customers of mitigation and ETA to full recovery. Ben/Triage: craft brief message for ACME and mailstream.

ben: Drafting: "We're investigating elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting some requests. We've applied throttles and routing fallbacks to reduce impact; service is recovering. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Sending now.

sre-runner: Ops note: consider a follow-up to implement automated KV eviction thresholds and reactive fallback for oversized-sequence requests. I'll file an action item.

carla: Agreed. Also include a change to enable eviction metrics and an alert if kv_cache.evictions==0 && kv_cache.size > 60GB for 5m.

dmitri: One outstanding item: a small percentage of realtime customers still seeing intermittent 5xx due to backlog on dedicated nodes (pool-7). I recommend scaling pool-7 by +2 nodes and draining heavy clients onto dedicated spare capacity. Anyone object?

emma: Go ahead. I'll trigger a scale.

ops-bot: SCALE ACTION: pool-7 scaled +2 nodes by emma at 1729993555. Expected ready ~2m.

carla: Thanks team. Current status: degraded but stabilizing. We'll keep the thread open until error rate <1% and queue length <200 for 15m. Postmortem owners assigned: dmitri (root cause), ben (customer comms), emma (metrics/alerts), carla (incident writeup).

sre-runner: Documented immediate action items in incident tracker.

carla: Closing loop for now. If anything regresses ping @carla directly. Otherwise I'll mark this as mitigated after observation window. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigations applied. monitoring window started at 1729993568.

ben: Thanks everyone, great execution.

dmitri: I'll write the RCA draft and share timeline.

emma: Metrics look stable: 5xx ~0.9%, queue length 120. Closing soon.

carla: Marking last message ts 1729993580 here for thread. We'll keep followups in the postmortem doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring. Tickets: #INC-2026-1729993333 created."
